title: Rigveda 1.75: To Agni
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 1.75: To Agni: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 1.75 is a hymn of 5 verses addressed to Agni. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 1, a collection of hymns by many families of poets. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 51v-52r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.text: <sup>1</sup>ACCEPT our loudest-sounding hymn, food most delightful to the Gods, Pouring our offerings in thy mouth.

translation.original_ref: RV 1.75.2-5 (aṣṭaka 1, adhyāya 5, varga 23); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 52r
translation.original_text:
2athā̍ te aṅgirasta̱māgne̍ vedhastama pri̱yam | vo̱cema̱ brahma̍ sāna̱si ||
3kas te̍ jā̱mir janā̍nā̱m agne̱ ko dā̱śva̍dhvaraḥ | ko ha̱ kasmi̍nn asi śri̱taḥ ||
4tvaṁ jā̱mir janā̍nā̱m agne̍ mi̱tro a̍si pri̱yaḥ | sakhā̱ sakhi̍bhya̱ īḍya̍ḥ ||
5yajā̍ no mi̱trāvaru̍ṇā̱ yajā̍ de̱vām̐ ṛ̱tam bṛ̱hat | agne̱ yakṣi̱ svaṁ dama̍m ||
translation.text:
2Now, Agni, will we say to thee, O wisest and best Angiras, Our precious, much-availing prayer.
3Who, Agni, is thy kin, of men? who is thy worthy worshipper? On whom dependent? who art thou?
4The kinsman, Agni, of mankind, their well beloved Friend art thou, A Friend whom friends may supplicate.
5Bring to us Mitra, Varuṇa, bring the Gods to mighty sacrifice. Bring them, O Agni, to thine home.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 52r (OPenn image 53, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 1.75.2 ‹-sānasi›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 52v, begins in RV 1.76.5 ‹-eva hotariti satya-tara tvam›. Verses 1.75.2-5 end on this page; 1.75.2 begins on fol. 51v.
translation.edition_text:
2atha | te | aṅgiraḥ-tama | agne | vedhaḥ-tama | priyam | vocema | brahma | sānasi
3kaḥ | te | jāmiḥ | janānām | agne | kaḥ | dāśu-adhvaraḥ | kaḥ | ha | kasmin | asi | śritaḥ
4tvam | jāmiḥ | janānām | agne | mitraḥ | asi | priyaḥ | sakhā | sakhi-bhyaḥ | īḍyaḥ
5yaja | naḥ | mitrāvaruṇā | yaja | devān | ṛtam | bṛhat | agne | yakṣi | svam | damam
